correctness.rationale: For each rotation, invariant domain and range have common size divisible by the rotational cycle length; exactly k cyclic shifts commute, giving R. For each reflection, the numbers of fixed selected vertices agree and exactly gcd(2,k) cyclic shifts intertwine the induced reflections, giving H. This covers all 2n automorphisms and proves every coefficient via Burnside. Vandermonde yields the divisor total; identity and reflection-fixed counts imply the next-to-unit formula, and nonidentity fixed-set bounds yield the asymptotic. The packaged Python checker exhaustively compares every rank-wise fixed count with actual partial maps for n=3..7, constructs actual orbits for n=3..6, and confirms arithmetic identities through n=18. The infinite proof is independent of these finite computations.

originality.rationale: The primary 2022 classification supplies the full dihedral automorphism group, while the 2011 enumeration supplies labeled rank counts, not the dihedral automorphism orbit quotient. Inspected adjacent published findings respectively concern maximal nilpotent chains in the same monoid and involutions in a strictly smaller dihedral-restriction inverse monoid; neither covers all conjugation orbits in every rank. Concrete rank-by-rank orbit counts and the next-to-unit orbit law are not direct consequences of the labeled counts. Priority remains qualified by inaccessible original 2000 presentation and possible general cycle-index literature.
residual_risks: No exhaustive global literature-priority guarantee; a general cycle-index theorem applied to cyclic-order partial bijections might give equivalent formulas.

value.rationale: The object is a standard inverse monoid with established algebraic automorphism group; the requested invariant is the natural classification of its elements by internal symmetries. The count in every rank is not the known labeled monoid census and detects nontrivial rotational/reflection stabilizers, with distinct even-odd reflection behavior. A sharp \(\binom n2+1\) orbit theorem at next-to-full rank and an exponential generic-freeness limit quantify nontrivial structural aspects for all n, rather than a small table or ad hoc slice.
